31.description:

If the move's intended target also has this ability, the move is not redirected. When multiple Pokémon with this ability are possible targets for redirection, the move is redirected to the one with the highest Speed stat, or, in the case of a tie, to a random tied Pokémon. Follow Me takes precedence over this ability.

If the Pokémon is a Ground-type and thus immune to Electric moves, its immunity prevents the Special Attack boost.

32.name: Serene Grace
32.effect: Doubles the chance of moves' extra effects occurring.
32.description:
In Scrambled Scarlet:
I only give Pokemon Serene Grace if they have some consistent, 100% guaranteed options for moves. The most important one is Revelation Dance, which now has a 100% chance to boost Sp. Atk with Serene Grace. Every Pokemon I've chosen to give Serene Grace fits enough to learn Revelation Dance. The other more important moves for the player are Moonblast and Play Rough, which will ALWAYS drop both offensive stats with Serene Grace. Sky Attack ALWAYS flinches (and gives +1 Atk/Accuracy) but has 1 PP. There are several of other moves with guaranteed effects with Serene Grace, including ones like Seed Flare, Eternal Beam, Flash Cannon, etc- which have guaranteed chances to drop Sp. Def with Serene Grace. This is less relevant for the player since the AI isn't hard switching 24/7, so the drops, while nice, are nothing crazy. Lastly, you can still try and Paraflinch cheese, but it's still inherently RNG reliant, even if it's heavily in the haxers favor.

This Pokémon's moves have twice their usual effect chance.

An effect chance is a move's chance to inflict a status ailment, cause a stat change, or make the target flinch in addition to the move's main effect. For example, Flamethrower's chance of burning the target is doubled, but Protect's chance of success and Air Cutter's increased critical hit rate are unaffected.

Secret Power is unaffected.

55.name: Hustle
55.effect: Strengthens physical moves to inflict 1.5× damage, but decreases their accuracy to 0.8×.
55.description:
In Scrambled Scarlet:
Wide Lens now gives a 25% accuracy boost, so 100% accurate moves won't miss with Hustle. The VAST majority of moves in this hack are 100% accurate. When Wide Lens used with Hustle, the accuracy check is negated unless the move is incarrute too. This makes fast Hustle Pokemon very good, essentially giving them a Choice Band but being able to switch moves in exchange for your ability slot. In addition to the accuracy boosting moves below, Rock Polish NOW gives +2 Speed AND Accuracy. Additionally, many moves now bypass the Hustle accuracy check outright. Below, I will list only the relevant non-missing moves that Pokemon with Hustle can learn. Standard Priority: Quick Attack - Accelerock - Aerial Ace - Ice Shard - Seed Shot - Aqua Jet - Befuddle Misc. Priority: Fake Out - Extreme Speed - First Impression - Sucker Punch - Grassy Glide 1 PP Priority Flinch Moves: Hold Back (+1 Atk/Sp. Atk/Acc) | Grav Apple (+1 Acc) Sky Attack/Focus Punch = +1 Accuracy/Atk | Dive/Smart Strike = +1 Accuracy U-Turn/Flip Turn | Avalanche/Payback | Heavy Slam/Heat Crash | Flail/Reversal Stomping Tantrum - Trop Kick - Triple Kick - Beat Up - Lash Out - Acrobatics - Solar Blade - Last Resort - Lunge - Finishing Blow

98.name: Magic Guard
98.effect: Protects against damage not directly caused by a move.
98.description:
This Pokémon is immune to damage not directly caused by a move.

For example, this Pokémon takes no damage from from weather, recoil, status ailments, or Spikes, but it still suffers from the Attack cut when burned, and a Life Orb will still power up this Pokémon's moves without damaging it. Anything that directly depends on such damage will also not happen; for example, Leech Seed will neither hurt this Pokémon nor heal the opponent, and Pokémon with a Jaboca Berry or Rowap Berry will not consume the berry when hit by this Pokémon.

The following are unaffected: Struggle, Pain Split (whether used by or against this Pokémon), Belly Drum, Substitute, Curse, moves that knock the user out, and damage from confusion.

This Pokémon will neither lose nor regain HP if it drains HP from a Pokémon with Liquid Ooze.

If this Pokémon is badly poisoned, the poison counter is still increased each turn; if the Pokémon loses this ability, it will begin taking as much damage as it would be if it had been taking increasing damage each turn.

99.name: Royal Decree

No Guard: Moves used by or against this Pokémon never miss.

One-hit KO moves are unaffected. Moves affected by this ability can hit Pokémon during the preparation turn of moves like Dig or Fly.

Overworld: If the lead Pokémon has this ability, the wild encounter rate is doubled.

101.name: Technician
101.effect: Strengthens moves of 60 base power or less to 1.5× their power.
101.description:
In Scrambled Scarlet:
Technician has too many moves for me to list here here. Check the move sheet for them. There are dozens of new Technician boosted priority moves, multi-hit moves, crit moves, stat boosting moves, and just general useful moves. I reccomend just going to the move sheet since I've already organized it all into easy to navigate categories so you can check them for yourself over there.

This Pokémon's moves have 1.5× their power if their base power is 60 or less.

This includes moves of variable power, such as Hidden Power and Magnitude, when their power is 60 or less. Helping Hand's power boost is taken into account for any move, as is Defense Curl's power boost for Rollout.

104.name: Mold Breaker
104.effect: Bypasses targets' abilities if they could hinder or prevent a move.
104.description:
This Pokémon's moves completely ignore abilities that could hinder or prevent their effect on the target.

For example, this Pokémon's moves ignore abilities that would fully negate them, such as Water Absorb; abilities that would prevent any of their effects, such as Clear Body, Shell Armor, or Sticky Hold; and abilities that grant any general protective benefit, such as Simple, Snow Cloak, or Thick Fat. If an ability could either hinder or help this Pokémon's moves, e.g. Dry Skin or Unaware, the ability is ignored either way.

Abilities that do not fit this description, even if they could hinder moves in some other way, are not affected. For example, Cursed Body only affects potential future uses of the move, while Liquid Ooze and Shadow Tag can only hinder a move's effect on the user. This ablity cannot ignore type or form changes granted by abilities, for example Color Change or Forecast; nor effects that were caused by abilities but are no longer tied to an ability, such as the rain from Drizzle. This ability cannot ignore Multitype at all.

An ability ignored by this ability is only nullified while the move is being used. For example, this Pokémon's moves can paralyze a Pokémon with Limber, but Limber will activate and heal the paralysis immediately thereafter, and this Pokémon's Spikes are not affected by this ability after they have been placed.

When this Pokémon enters battle, all participating trainers are notified that it has this ability.

This ability functions identically to Teravolt and Turboblaze.

105.name: Super Luck
105.effect: Raises moves' critical hit rates one stage.
105.description: This Pokémon's moves have critical hit rates one stage higher than normal.

109.name: Unaware

109.description:
This Pokémon ignores other Pokémon's stat modifiers for the purposes of damage and accuracy calculation.

The power of Punishment and Stored Power is calculated as usual. When this Pokémon hurts itself in confusion, its stat modifiers affect damage as usual.

114.name: Storm Drain
114.effect: Redirects single-target Water moves to this Pokémon where possible. Absorbs Water moves, raising Special Attack one stage.
114.description:
All other Pokémon's single-target Water-type moves are redirected to this Pokémon, if it is an eligible target. Other Pokémon's Water moves raise this Pokémon's Special Attack one stage, negating any other effect on it, and cannot miss it.

If the move's intended target also has this ability, the move is not redirected. When multiple Pokémon with this ability are possible targets for redirection, the move is redirected to the one with the highest Speed stat, or, in the case of a tie, to a random tied Pokémon. Follow Me takes precedence over this ability.

116.name: Solid Rock
116.effect: Decreases damage taken from super-effective moves by 1/4.

This Pokémon takes 0.75× as much damage from moves that are super effective against it.

117.description:
The weather changes to hail when this Pokémon enters battle and does not end unless cancelled by another weather condition.

If multiple Pokémon with this ability, Drizzle, Drought, or Sand Stream are sent out at the same time, the abilities will activate in order of Speed, respecting Trick Room. Each ability's weather will cancel the previous weather, and only the weather summoned by the slowest of the Pokémon will stay.

120.name: Reckless
120.effect: Strengthens recoil moves to 1.2× their power.
120.description:
In Scrambled Scarlet:
Reckless boosts recoil by 20%. 120 BP becomes 144 BP, 100 BP becomes 120. Click this link HERE to see all of the recoil moves in the game. There are many new ones.

This Pokémon's recoil moves and crash moves have 1.2× their base power.

123.name: Bad Dreams

123.description: Opposing Pokémon take 1/8 of their maximum HP in damage after each turn while they are asleep.

125.name: Sheer Force
125.effect: Strengthens moves with extra effects to 1.3× their power, but prevents their extra effects.
125.description:
In Scrambled Scarlet:
Sheer Force has dozens of new moves that affect it. Again, too many for it to be worth listing them. Most moves now have new effects, and many have additional effects. Many of these are guaranteed, useful, reliable effects- others are chance based which favors the AI, not the Nuzlocker where the stakes are higher and you shouldn't bank on RNG. Check bulbapedia for a full list of rules of Sheer Force- it's a pretty buggy, strange ability. As a general, simplified guide for what moves are boosted, here you go: If the move: Can status the opponent, flinch, drop or raise a stat of yourself/foe (unless it's dropping your own stats)- it's boosted.

This Pokémon's moves with extra effects have 1.3× their power, but lose their extra effects.

An effect chance is a move's chance to inflict a status ailment, cause a stat change, or make the target flinch in addition to the move's main effect. For example, Thunder Shock's paralysis is an extra effect, but Thunder Wave's is not, nor are Knock Off's item removal and Air Cutter's increased critical hit rate.

Moves that lower the user's stats are unaffected.

126.name: Contrary
126.description:
In Scrambled Scarlet:
Click HERE to see all of the new Draco Meteor variants and Close Combat variants. Obviously, these synergize very well with Contrary, being 120-140 BP and giving insane stat boosts. Because of this, I was very stingy when giving this ability out. In general, I tend to dislike how this ability functions with these new moves, but I like it on a specific few Pokemon since they might feel a bit boring/underwhelming lategame otherwise, and since the ability fits them well. None of them are fast enough to completely sweep unless they hold a Scarf, and even then sweeping is not necessarily brainless due to the way I structure trainer sets and items/moves on those trainers. Some lategame fights depending on the matchup and prep can be cheesed with Contrary regardless, though.
